NEW DELHI: The AIADMK on Monday took a swipe at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his visit to London to attract investment, questioning the need for such an overseas trip at taxpayers’ expense.The party pointed out that a company established in India in 1986 and headquartered in Noida was among the businesses involved, raising questions over the rationale for Vijay travelling to the UK for investment promotion."A company established in India on 1986 , HQ Noida @actorvijay travels all the way to UK at tax payers money to attract investment," AIADMK spokesperson Kovai Sathyan said in a post on X.Meanwhile, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Sunday also took a swipe at Vijay’s UK visit, saying that while the government projected it as an effort to attract investments, photographs from the trip told a different story.Speaking at the engagement ceremony of an AIADMK functionary in Trichy, Palaniswami indirectly referred to photographs of Vijay flagging off a motor race at Silverstone.“It was believed that he was going to bring investments and improve the state’s economy. However, the photographs published in today’s newspapers tell a different story. Decide for yourself what they represent,” he said.This comes as, Vijay on Monday highlighted a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed in London between Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd and Guidance, Tamil Nadu, for an investment of approximately Rs 11,000 crore in the state."Today (14.09.2026), in London, England, Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd., along with its European and UK-based joint venture companies, entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with Guidance, Tamil Nadu, for an investment of approximately Rs.11,000 crore in Tamil Nadu. This investment will create employment opportunities for around 7,000 people across sectors including design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and logistics facilities," Vijay said in a post on X.The MoU was signed and exchanged by Barry Painter, Global Head of Marketing and Communications, Samvardhana Motherson International Group, and Deepak Jacob, IAS, managing director of guidance, the nodal agency of the Tamil Nadu government.Indian high commissioner to the UK Kumaran Periyasamy, company representatives and senior Tamil Nadu government officials were also present at the event.Vijay is currently on a week-long visit to the United Kingdom as part of an overseas outreach programme aimed at attracting investments and expanding partnerships in sectors including advanced manufacturing, electric vehicles, electronics and Global Capability Centres.
Article Summary: The party pointed out that a company established in india in 1986 and headquartered in noida was among the businesses involved. Aiadmk general secretary edappadi k palaniswami also took a swipe at vijay’s uk visit, saying photographs from the trip told a different story.

Article Title: 'First step towards safety': Meta to report child sexual abuse cases to law enforcement
Article Text:
The development comes as the government continues to engage with social media platforms over harmful content and compliance with Indian laws

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Social media giant Meta on Tuesday agreed to report cases related to child sexual abuse to appropriate law enforcement agencies in India, government sources told ANI.The development comes as the government continues to engage with social media platforms over harmful content and compliance with Indian laws. Government sources told ANI that the online safety of children is a “fundamental principle” for any social media platform operating in India and is “non-negotiable”.“Meta has agreed to report child safety-related matters to the appropriate law enforcement agencies. It is a first step towards making the platforms safe for children, and much more needs to be done,” government sources told ANI.The government is also engaging with other platforms to ensure they proactively identify and remove harmful content, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), sources said. It warned that action would be taken against platforms that fail to take proactive steps to ensure the safety of children.The latest development follows a series of discussions between Meta and government officials over the company’s compliance with Indian laws and its content moderation systems.During earlier meetings, officials had sought details on Meta’s algorithms, content moderation mechanisms, compliance processes, checks and balances, and safeguards against CSAM and deepfake content.Government sources had said platforms could not operate in India solely according to US laws, stressing that they have a responsibility towards society and Indian law.The government had also raised questions over Meta’s eligibility for safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act. The provision protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content, subject to certain conditions.
Article Summary: The development comes as the government continues to engage with social media platforms over harmful content and compliance with indian laws. Government sources told ani that the online safety of children is a “fundamental principle’ for any social media platform operating in india.

NEW DELHI: A popular Indian travel vlogger from Kerala, who has been travelling in Afghanistan and posting videos from the country, on Monday claimed that she had been "arrested" by the "Mujahideen" in Bamyan and appealed for help in contacting the Indian embassy.In a post on her Facebook page, the vlogger, "Backpacker Arunima", shared what she described as a translation of an official communication from local authorities, stating that she had been arrested by the Mujahideen in Afghanistan."You were arrested by Mujahideen just now because you do not have an official letter," the translated message read."Backpacker Arunima" also appealed for assistance in reaching the Indian embassy."If you anyone know Indian embassy please contact," she wrote.The veracity of the post could not be independently ascertained, and there was no immediate response from the Ministry of External Affairs.The post offered no further details about the circumstances of her alleged arrest or identified those who had detained her.Arunima has been travelling across Afghanistan and has shared several videos from the country on her social media accounts. She has more than 1.2 million followers on Instagram and 2.39 lakh on Facebook, while her YouTube channel has over 7.3 lakh subscribers.According to her social media profiles, she has spent the past six years hitchhiking through remote routes and documenting "rare and risky" regions.

Article Title: You can buy a social media account. Or sell yours
Article Text:
When an account looks believable, it is something of a prize, but for those with legitimate or non-legitimate reasons.

Here a buyer can sort accounts by, among other things, price, follower count, and place of follower concentration.

A dedicated marketplace

An India-tagged Facebook account with 3 million subscribers on sale, a large market that's been operating since 2017

India remains the leading country after US as buyer on the sales sites.

Why does it feel shady?

India keeps showing up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

You could blame the bots. Someone’s asking for Rs 6.7 lakh to sell an India-based Instagram account with just 7,000 followers, a description that goes “Rajputi reel uploaded”, and 54 posts made in the one year it has existed.It’s a bit of an outsized ask, but not as preposterous as you might imagine. Social media accounts — entire accounts, not followers — have been bought and sold on grey markets for at least a decade and a half. The influencer economy helped. Once audiences could be monetised, followers and engagement acquired a fairly literal value. But, at the same time, bots made followers cheap and accounts easy to manufacture at scale. People could — and often still can — tell when it’s all fake. They may or may not care, but they can tell.So, when an account looks believable — with the odd little follower base, the awkward posts, and the occasional little viral bump — it is something of a prize.If someone wants the account for legitimate purposes, such as the launch of a new brand, it can shorten the wait to qualify for monetisation and other gated features.And if they want it for absolutely-not-legitimate reasons, such as scams, the account’s history gives them quicker (and easier) credibility.See the difference here.“I am from Patna, Bihar”, a profile on a marketplace says. And they’re offering a “3M Indian Facebook page for sale” — a Facebook page with 3 million followers. The asking price on the July listing is $4,500 — about Rs 4.3 lakh. It might almost seem like a bargain, given the large-ish following (but there’s also the declining page views whose screenshots the seller has added, perhaps in the spirit of transparency, to consider). It’s some $0.0015, about Re 0.14, per follower.The same seller also offered a “baby”-focused Facebook page with “10k followers organic views”, meaning the reach came without paid promotion, in Aug. The largest following is in India (39%), going by the screenshots posted in the listing, and it offers two valuable things. The first is “content monetisation”, meaning access to Facebook’s system for earning money from eligible content, which a new page would otherwise have to spend time building towards and qualifying for. The other is the ability to run the page “with your desired name”, meaning the page can be renamed and repurposed for a new brand or identity. For this small page, the seller is asking for $150 — a bit under Rs 14,400. This works out to about $0.015, or Rs 1.44, per follower.It’s a neat 10 times the asking price of the larger account, if we go purely by follower count.This means follower count isn’t really what is always being sold. The history, audience, activity, monetisation, and ability to repurpose the account can often matter much more. The original email, for instance, holds value because it can be part of the account-recovery trail, and buyers worry that a previous owner who retains it could later reclaim the account.It’s definitely much easier to ‘sell’ your social media account today than it was a decade ago. It’s not all crude or iffy websites and message boards anymore. There are dedicated marketplaces for buying and selling social media accounts that are incredibly organised.SeBuDA, where the Rs 6.7 lakh asking-price Instagram account is listed, is a good example. A buyer can sort accounts by price, follower count, the country and city where followers are concentrated, their gender, the account’s category and age, and whether the original email address comes with it. The listing itself often shows audience demographics, analytics, recent posts, engagement numbers — many of these screenshots — alongside seller history and escrow record. Accounts can even be put on a comparison list.Similarly, Fameswap — which has been around since 2013 and is now one of the biggest dedicated marketplaces for social media accounts — has a price-discovery mechanism. Its market insights data shows that YouTube accounts that put out reviews and how-to videos are priced the highest (a median asking price of more than $60 for every thousand followers). For TikTok accounts, the sweet spot is crypto and NFTs (about $40). And for Instagram accounts, it’s tech and science ($19).Another major market, DealBaron, has an even more formalised process. When a seller lists an account, the site pulls in basic account data and asks them to prove they control it by posting a generated code on that account. Buyers can see seller ratings and deal histories, make binding offers and, once a deal starts, follow a platform-specific handover process inside DealBaron.SWAPD, also a large market that has been operating since 2017, looks more like a forum than these sites, but the transactions are tightly managed — and “under continuous human supervision”, rather than through automated checkouts. SWAPD says it reviews listings before they go live, and that it requires sellers handling qualifying transactions to complete KYC identity checks.As for the money, most of these markets either offer or require escrow, where the buyer’s money is held by the platform or an escrow service until the account has been transferred.The way it works makes it easier for sellers to build inventories and for buyers to shop for exactly the sort of account they want. And, for a buyer, several smaller accounts might presumably make more sense than putting everything into one page with an enormous following: if one is suspended, reclaimed or lost, the entire “investment” doesn’t sink.First, the social media platforms whose accounts are being bought and sold largely don’t allow it. Instagram and X explicitly ban it. TikTok doesn’t allow it without permission, nor does Facebook. YouTube does allow ownership of a brand account to be transferred, but not in quite the same ways as these sales usually go. That doesn’t necessarily make selling an account illegal. It just makes much of this a grey market — the transaction can breach a platform’s rules without itself being a crime, although what buyers or sellers do with the account certainly can be.Which brings us to the second point, that these are clearly not markets populated only by people selling one old account that they don’t use anymore. Many sellers list bundles of multiple accounts (a seller, for instance, announced they had an “unlimited stock” of “active” Instagram accounts for sale at one point). And markets have sometimes actively intervened to block the sale of stolen accounts.The first large-scale academic study of such social media marketplaces, published in 2025, found more than 38,000 accounts advertised for sale across 11 marketplaces, with asking prices adding up to more than $64 million.And it found evidence that “these marketplaces foster fraudulent activities such as bot farming, harvesting accounts for future fraud, and fraudulent engagement”. “The ecosystem of buying and selling social media profiles fosters cybercriminals to operate at scale, making it easy to obtain accounts to launch various cybercrime activities,” it found.Of the nearly 11,500 for-sale accounts the researchers could examine, almost 3,800 had posted scams — with nearly 19,000 posts with crypto scams, phishing, fake products and services, impersonation, and other fraud. And 30% of “sold accounts” they could date had been created before 2020, “leveraging their longevity to evade detection”.The researchers also found signs that accounts were being deliberately built for resale — given plausible names, bios and locations, and grown with enough followers and activity to make them look like genuine and naturally used accounts, rather than obvious fakes. Some sellers seemed to produce these accounts as inventory, replacing listings with new ones as others disappeared.An Aug 2026 study of YouTube accounts sold on a single account marketplace also found that channels weren’t necessarily being bought for what they already were. More than 1,000 of the 4,600-odd channels they tracked — 23% — were repurposed, their handles, titles and descriptions changed into something essentially new.But changing identities, weirdly, didn’t make the audience flee. Over the 12 weeks after repurposing, “subscriber counts increase on average — often substantially”, perhaps because, as the researchers put it, “most users remain unaware of the change and stay subscribed”.FT reported in Aug that the trade has developed its own supply chain, with suppliers sourcing accounts, flippers reselling them and editors helping turn them into something new. In one case, a 3,90,000-follower Instagram account sold for $6,000 and its new owner said it made about $2,000 from sponsorships and sales in its first two weeks alone.The 2025 study had found that of the accounts whose public profiles revealed a location, India was the second-most common country — after the US.When another set of researchers studied the closely related business of selling followers, likes and other engagement in 2024, India was one of the biggest hubs there as well. The researchers found the business was cheap to enter and English-speaking Indian operators could enter the global market easily. Just like those from other “former British colonies” like Bangladesh, Nigeria, Malaysia, or a former US colony like the Philippines.But they admitted they knew “very little” about the differences between countries.On the major marketplaces, India is a large source of traffic. Data from web analytics platform Semrush for July 2026 shows India accounted for the third highest traffic on SeBuDA and a similar marketplace SocialTradia, and the second highest on SWAPD and Fameswap.Threads on SWAPD, in fact, keep discussing Indian sellers (for instance, how they drive prices down) and buyers (for instance, how they can drive the value of India-heavy accounts up). It can get so India-coded that a Reddit account seller said on a Jan listing: “Indian buyer preferred because payments are just easier with UPI.”SWAPD itself posted in March this year that India was tied with the US for the largest group among its 40 highest-volume operators.India, clearly, is becoming a significant part of this market.
Article Summary: An india-tagged facebook account with 3 million subscribers on sale, a large market that's been operating since 2017. When an account looks believable, it is something of a prize, but for those with legitimate or non-legitimate reasons. Sebuda, where the rs 6.7 lakh asking-price instagram account is listed, is a good example.

Article Title: Aryna Sabalenka’s investment lands $1 billion in funding as she reels from 2026 US Open heartbreak
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka's investment.(Image via Getty Images)

Aryna Sabalenka’s investment gets a $1 billion in funding as she remains focused on her career amid the 2026 US Open heartbreak

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aryna Sabalenka’s net worth has increased significantly as she becomes one of the highest paid tennis players in the world

Aryna Sabalenka, the 28 year old Belarusian professional tennis star who currently holds the World No. 2 ranking in women's singles by the Women's Tennis Association, is currently with the loss against Elena Rybakina, in three sets: 6–4, 5–7, 6–2, in the 2026 US Open. Amid this, her investment in a brand has sparked chaos after it received a whopping $1 billion in funding.Aryna Sabalenka is a global ambassador and equity shareholder in IM8 Health, a y growing premium longevity and nutritional supplement brand which has been co-founded by David Beckham and parent company Prenetics Global.The 28 year old tennis star has been associated with the profitable brand for over a year now after she invested in it in June 2025. As per reports, just a few weeks ago, it was announced that the brand IM8 has taken on $1 billion in funding from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF),Adit Swarup, a partner at General Catalyst and lead on the CVF partnership with Prenetics Global issued a statement that read as, “IM8 is a category-defining consumer health business, and the underlying cohort economics are among the strongest we’ve seen across the Customer Value Fund portfolio…”The statement added, “Their cohort retention data is remarkable: highly consistent across geographies, subscription tenors, and product lines, with quarterly renewal rates setting new industry benchmarks for direct-to-consumer health.”Prenetics Global co-founding partner & CEO Danny Yeung weighed in on adding Aryna Sabalenka as he said her coach, Jason Stacy, had recommended her to try it out.Prenetics Global co-founding partner & CEO Danny Yeung said, “Of course, Jason does a lot of vetting before he gives anything to Aryna first…She started taking it and she actually felt different in terms of energy, endurance, cognitive function, et cetera...Her agent [Evolve’s Stuart Duguid] got in touch and said, ‘You know what, Aryna really likes the product, she’s been taking the product, and she only endorses things that she really believes in and uses herself every day. ’ That’s where the conversation got started.”While Aryna Sabalenka has not spoken of her investment in public yet, she has been pretty active with investments in growing startups.Apart from IM8, the tennis star has also acquired equity stakes in the prebiotic soda brand Olipop and the propolis-based wellness company Beekeeper's Naturals.According to Forbes, Aryna Sabalenka’s net worth is a whopping $22 million as she is the 4th highest paid tennis player in the world.While the 28 year old star keeps her focus on the court, it seems her investments have grown rapidly.
Article Summary: Aryna sabalenka’s investment gets a $1 billion in funding as she remains focused on her career amid the 2026 us open heartbreak. The 28 year old tennis star has been associated with the profitable brand for over a year now after she invested in it in june 2025.

Article Title: Apple bundles TV, Arcade with iCloud+; ends standalone Apple One subscriptions in India
Article Text: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost, combining cloud storage, video streaming and gaming in a single subscription.Apple is also introducing Apple Select, a new service integrated into the existing Apple Music app, exclusively for iCloud+ subscribers. This addition extends the expanded bundle’s benefits to the music app, offering subscribers an exclusive collection of music.The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Subscribers can share the package with up to five family members. The rollout will take place through September.The change will end standalone Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions sold directly by Apple in India. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+. Apple said access would remain uninterrupted and Arcade game progress and saves would be preserved.Apple One, which bundles several Apple services, will also close to new subscribers in India.Existing subscribers will retain their subscriptions. This means new customers seeking Apple’s combined storage and entertainment offering will be directed towards iCloud+, while current Apple One users can continue with their existing package.Apple One currently has two plans in India: Individual at Rs 195 a month, with 50GB of iCloud+ storage, and Family at Rs 365 a month, with 200GB, shareable with up to five other family members. Both include Apple Music, Apple TV and Apple Arcade. Apple Music is not included in the newly announced iCloud+ bundle, a key distinction for users comparing the offerings.The shift turns cloud storage, often bought when free space runs out, into an entry point for Apple’s entertainment services. For existing iCloud+ customers, the immediate benefit is access to streaming and games without an additional subscription bill.For Apple, bundling could help expose more paying customers to services they may not have chosen separately. It also gives users another reason to retain their storage subscription. However, customers who want only Apple TV or Arcade will now have to take the combined offering when subscribing directly through Apple.“We’re excited to bring Apple TV and Apple Arcade to iCloud+ users in over 100 countries in one convenient subscription,” said Eddy Cue, Apple’s senior vice president of Services and Health.Airtel customers with iPhones can also access the expanded subscription through eligible postpaid plans. Those already receiving Apple TV through select Airtel plans can transition at no additional cost. Availability of individual features, shows and games may vary by country, region or device.
Article Summary: Starting this month, icloud+ subscribers will get apple tv and apple arcade at no additional cost. The expanded service will start at rs 75 a month for 50gb of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through icloud+.

Article Text:

Marc Benioff: No conditions for donation schools, except one

Bringing the 1-1-1 model to schools

Salesforce has announced $27 million in new education grants nationwide, including $18 million directly supporting public school districts in San Francisco, Oakland, New York City, Chicago, and Indianapolis. The new funding is said to build on 14 years of partnership with public schools and reflects Salesforce’s continued and growing commitment to supporting schools, educators, and students. Announced ahead of Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference, the grants come alongside an expanded focus on education across the company.The latest donation marks the continuation of an effort launched in 2013, when Salesforce CEO and founder Marc Benioff wrote an initial $2.7 million check as a down payment on a decade-long, $100 million pledge. Over the years, Benioff sustained and expanded the initiative, which he claimed represents more funding than any company has given in history and provides consequential support to local public classrooms.Himself a San Francisco resident, in his growing up years, Benioff emphasizes that the money comes without mandates on district policy. He said that the only condition is that there is “no hate, no discrimination” and the grants focus on quality and sustainability.The program pairs capital with direct labor under the company's 1-1-1 philanthropic model, which dedicates 1% each of equity, product, and employee time to charitable causes. Days before the fall term began, high-ranking executives joined staff members on campuses to prepare classrooms.On the latest gift Benioff said, “At Salesforce, we believe business is the greatest platform for change.” He added, “That’s why we created the 1-1-1 model of giving back and built it into our culture from Day One, and it’s why we’ve continued to invest in our communities, in our hometown of San Francisco, and in our public schools for nearly three decades. As AI transforms our world, we have an even greater responsibility to support schools and teachers and help make sure every young person has the opportunity to thrive. When we bring together our financial resources, our technology, and the time and expertise of our employees, we can make an incredible impact.”Beyond classroom preparation and unrestricted $100,000 checks provided to every middle school principal, the Chronicle reported that the scope of the grants has evolved alongside technological shifts. The funding historically targeted computer science access and math instruction, but recent disbursements have increasingly addressed the rise of artificial intelligence. In partnership with groups such as aiEDU, the initiative helps educators establish responsible usage policies and train students for future workplace demands.For more than 27 years, Salesforce’s 1-1-1 model is claimed to have guided the company’s philanthropy, committing 1% of equity, technology, and employee time to giving back. As per the company, "Since its founding, the company has provided $970 million in grants, employees have contributed nearly 11 million volunteer hours, and 65,300 nonprofits and educational institutions use Salesforce technology for free or at a discount. "In a release, Salesforce said that this year the company is bringing that model into "schools through a relaunched Adopt-a-School program across more than 25 public schools nationwide, including 15 middle schools in the Bay Area. The program pairs employees and senior executives with schools to build ongoing relationships and provide hands-on support based on what schools need most, from mentoring students and leading workshops to setting up classrooms and refreshing school spaces. Salesforce has already reached its first-year goal of over 25 adopted schools and plans to expand the program globally in FY28."

The new funding is said to build on 14 years of partnership with public schools and reflects salesforce’s continued and growing commitment to supporting schools, educators, and students.

Article Title: Michael Dell to Goldman Sachs investors: Customers sort of go through five stages of grief, starting with OK ...
Article Text:
Dell's strategy to deal with supply chain shortages

'CEOs and managers are still figuring out the AI advantage'

The global semiconductor crunch fueling higher compute and Personal Computer (PC) prices across the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is poised to intensify further over the next few years, according to Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell. Speaking to investors at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference recently, founder of PC giant Dell warned that industry-wide supply bottlenecks will "probably" be worse in 2027 than in 2026, CRN reported.Dell explained to Goldman Sachs analyst Katherine Murphy that the rapid leap from basic Large Language Models (LLMs) to complex reasoning engines and autonomous agents has vastly outstripped manufacturing lead times. According to him, since this progress unfolded far faster than the years required to construct a new semiconductor fabrication plant, a deep structural shortage has emerged. While rising component and memory costs are systematically passed along to buyers, Dell noted that customers ultimately move past initial pricing pushback because an inability to source hardware poses an existential threat to running their operations."Yes, costs are going up. Yes, we price all that through. But you know customers sort of go through five stages of grief (saying initially), ‘OK the price went up I don’t really like that.’ You know what is worse than that? They don’t have availability. Because they can’t run their business and that is a disaster.”Once customers come to grips with the higher costs of infrastructure, Dell said they ask, “Are you going to be able to supply us with what we need over the next year or two years? So that is what we work on with our customers. We watch closely for any signs of double ordering or things that are not being utilized and we don’t see that.”To navigate the squeeze, the tech giant is actively monitoring its order pipeline to verify that equipment is genuinely deployed rather than stockpiled. Dell emphasized to investors that his company commands the best demand-signal integrity in the market due to its direct engagement with end users. Dell told Goldman Sachs investors, “We are more directly working with customers of all types and we see what the actual demand is from the end customers. ” He noted that historically tighter supply environments have worked to Dell’s advantage, citing longstanding supplier partnerships and a vast product catalog that enables the firm to dynamically allocate components where customer appetite is strongest.Beyond immediate logistics, semiconductor manufacturers view the company as a dependable counterparty capable of absorbing high-capital-expenditure fab output across long horizons stretching into the late 2030s. Dell highlighted that enterprise buyers equally rely on the hardware maker to honor its delivery commitments during turbulent cycles. At the same time, enterprise appetite shows little sign of dampening, with executive leadership increasingly viewing AI deployment not as a traditional IT expense, but as a critical driver of efficiency, innovation, and direct corporate value creation. He said, “If you had 200 people doing something now you can have 50 people doing the same thing with $10 million of AI spend and it costs half as much and it actually works better. So what’s happening is the CEOs and the business line executives are all figuring out they need AI to be more competitive, to be more innovative, to be faster. So the conversation is sort of leaving the traditional budget discussion because this is actually how you create value inside companies."
Article Summary: Dell technologies ceo michael dell warned that industry-wide supply bottlenecks will "probably" be worse in 2027 than in 2026. Dell emphasized to investors that his company commands the best demand-signal integrity in the market due to its direct engagement with end users.

Article Title: Apple rolls out its biggest iPhone software update of 2026: 10 ways iOS 27 will 'change' your iPhone
Article Text:
Apple's iOS 27 is out for iPhone 11 and newer, with Siri AI as the headline change.

iOS 27 compatible iPhones: the list stretches back to 2019

iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max

The complete iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 lines, including the 16e and 17e

iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo

iPhone SE, second generation onward

How to update to iOS 27

Back up first through Settings, your name, iCloud Backup, Back Up Now. Use a computer instead if your iCloud storage has run out.

Open Settings, General, Software Update. Swipe down on the page if iOS 27 is not showing yet.

Select iOS 27 and follow the prompts. A number of users have watched the installer describe itself as 26.7 before the phone reboots onto iOS 27.

Switch Siri AI on afterwards in Settings. It stays off until you ask for it, and it is not available to anyone under 13.

Siri AI knows what is in your inbox, and answers from it

Finding a mail, message, photo, link or file by person, date or place

Building a home automation from an instruction such as locking every door at midnight

Adding a birthday or a second number to a contact without opening the app

Lifting every ingredient off a recipe page into a shopping list

Answering questions about whatever is on screen, and searching the web when it has to

Point the camera at a restaurant bill and Siri splits it

Write with Siri copies your tone before it writes a word

Older iPhones feel quicker, and Liquid Glass gets a dial

Shortcuts builds the automation from one sentence

Photos can extend a shot past the edges of the frame

Safari watches a product page and tells you when the price falls

AirPods finally get a custom EQ, alarms get their own volume

A child now has to ask before opening a new website

Ask to Buy holds every app install until a parent says yes

Ask to Browse does the same for new websites in Safari, with the request arriving in the parent's Messages

Communication Safety, which already caught nudity, now intervenes on gore and violence in shared images and video

Time Allowances cap daily use across Entertainment, Games and Social Media, with age guidance Apple developed with clinical and child development specialists, while Schedules decide which apps work at which hours

One phone number across two iPhones, for a monthly fee

The smaller iOS 27 changes are the ones you will stumble into

Save a single frame from a video as a photo, instead of screenshotting and cropping it. Anyone who shoots video of moving children or pets has wanted this for years.

A Captured By Me filter in Photos separates pictures you actually took from the flood of forwards in your library, reaching back across older iPhones.

Wallet builds a pass from a photograph of a physical card, so a library card or a gift voucher stops living in a drawer. There is a manual template route if your iPhone does not support Apple Intelligence.

Home screen widgets stretch to an extra large size, which makes Notes, Calendar and Weather worth reading rather than tapping through. Weather now shows nine days instead of five.

Choose which eight controls sit above the Camera viewfinder. Lens Aperture and Shutter Speed are reserved for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

Messages stops holding up your next text while a large photo crawls out over weak cellular.

Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year, and it is free for every iPhone 11 and newer. The rollout started on Monday and the update is live in India now. The headline is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers. Underneath that sit a Camera app that can read a restaurant bill, a Shortcuts app you can talk into shape, a Photos editor that pushes a picture past its own borders, and a slider for everyone who spent the last year quietly resenting Liquid Glass.Siri AI is also the feature Apple has owed its users since 2024. The personalised, context aware assistant it demonstrated that year never shipped on schedule, and the gap was long enough that a fair number of iPhone owners stopped waiting and installed a chatbot instead. What arrives today is that promise, delivered late and still carrying a beta label, with English first and French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish following in October.Apple has hedged the rest of the release accordingly. A great deal of engineering in iOS 27 has gone into things that have nothing to do with AI, from app launch times to how the phone hands over between Wi-Fi and cellular, which is the part of this update that will reach the most people.iOS 27 installs on:Apple Intelligence and Siri AI need a shorter list: iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model and later, the iPhone Air and the iPhone Duo. A handful of features sit on an even narrower shelf. Tuning how Siri sounds, down to pitch and pace, is restricted to the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Duo, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and Air.The new assistant works like a chatbot with one thing no rival has, which is private access to what is already on the phone. When you install the update it indexes your calendar invites, mail, texts, files and notes, then answers from that. Ask for a recent photo of your dog and it surfaces several. Ask which weekend you were in Goa and it knows, because your boarding passes told it. The working list includes:Say the wake word and a shimmering orb appears in the Dynamic Island with a card you can pull down into a full Siri app, which keeps your conversations and continues them on an iPad. It now asks which part of a request it did not follow rather than failing silently. It is still slower to respond than Gemini, and it fumbles retrievals a well indexed inbox should make easy.Swipe past Photo and Video in the Camera app and a Siri tab appears. Hold it over a nutrition label and the numbers go into Health. Hold it over a shopfront and ask for the hours. Hold it over an event schedule and each entry lands in your calendar. The demo everyone will run is the receipt split, which reads the bill, works out each person's share with tax and tip, and settles the total through Apple Cash. Printed receipts scan reliably. Handwriting is a gamble. The Apple Cash requirement also means this is a feature Indian users can admire and not use.Siri can draft inside any text field, rewrite what you have typed, shift the register, or tell you where a draft is weak. In Messages and Mail it reads your existing writing and imitates your phrasing and punctuation, which is the difference between a useful draft and one you delete. Grammar suggestions now appear alongside spelling corrections across the system.Apple's own testing puts app launches up to 30 per cent faster, newly shot photos loading up to 70 per cent faster in the library, and AirDrop transfers up to 80 per cent faster. Treat the figures as the company's, but the change registers within minutes, and it lands on every supported handset instead of only the Apple Intelligence tier. Messages retries a failed send by itself now, and the switch between Wi-Fi and cellular is less jarring. For the look of the thing, Settings, Appearance, Liquid Glass opens a slider that runs from ultra clear to fully tinted.Shortcuts has always been capable and almost nobody used it, because building anything meant stacking actions by hand and guessing at the logic. Now you tap the plus sign, write what you want, and the app assembles it. Message a family member your ETA when you leave the office, or trigger a playlist when CarPlay connects. You can refine the result in plain language or edit the steps yourself.Clean Up has been the softest of Apple's editing tools since it launched, mostly because it left warped patches behind. It now runs in three modes: Fast, on device, for small removals, High Quality, which goes to Apple's servers, and Auto. Beside it are Extend, which invents what lies past the original frame, and Spatial Reframing, which shifts the apparent camera position after the picture was taken. Image Playground handles photorealistic output now, and Apple has said SynthID watermarking support is coming later this year.Notify Me is the smartest small idea in this release. Find the listing in Safari, open the Tab bar menu, tap Notify Me, describe the change you are waiting for and set how often the browser should check. It watches the page for a restock or a price cut and alerts you. Safari also sorts open tabs into topics on its own, and will write a custom extension from a plain description, from a citation generator to forcing a minimum font size on a site with unreadable type.You can tune the lows, mids and highs on AirPods yourself rather than accepting Apple's preset, through AirPods settings, Audio and Routing, Equaliser, Custom. It works on AirPods 4 and 5, AirPods Pro 2 and 3, and AirPods Max 2. Separately, Settings, Sounds and Haptics lets you unlink alarm volume from ringer volume, which fixes the old problem of sleeping through an alarm or being startled by a notification at maximum volume. GymKit also arrives on iPhone, and AirPods Pro 3 can pass heart rate data into a workout.The parental controls are the most substantial non AI work in this release, and they are built around approval rather than blocking:Screen Time itself has been redesigned around an at a glance view of what a child actually used.Two iPhones running iOS 27 can share a single number, with the line following whichever handset you unlock. It is set up in Settings, Cellular, This iPhone and Another. The obstacle is the carrier. Only T-Mobile supports it at launch, at roughly Rs 440 a month, with Verizon expected later this year and no Indian operator involved yet.Some of the best work in this update never made a slide. These are the fixes that remove a daily irritation rather than add a headline, and most of them land on older iPhones too.The bigger leftovers come with conditions attached. Call Context surfaces a confirmation code or a booking reference from your mail while you are on a call to a business. HomeKit Secure Video cameras record and stream in 4K, and the Home app can describe what happened in a clip or search footage in plain language, although those AI pieces need a 2TB iCloud+ plan for a single camera and more beyond that. Maps Flyover renders architectural detail and individual trees from aerial imagery. Cycle Tracking in Health adds perimenopause support, with deviation notifications aimed at users over 40. iCloud Shared Albums allow full resolution sharing at last, and are easier to join from Android or Windows. VoiceOver and Magnifier both pick up substantial accessibility work.One to wait for rather than look for: the Passwords app will update weak or compromised logins on your behalf, but Apple has marked that as coming in a future release rather than shipping it today.
Article Summary: Apple has released ios 27, the largest iphone software update it has shipped all year. The rollout started on monday and the update is live in india now. The headline change is siri ai, a rebuilt assistant that reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights.
